last_material_result: One bounded feasibility/economics round KILLED Seoul Tomorrow Commute Disruption Digest. A genuinely useful saved-corridor product needs repeat delivery and user-specific corridor state; removing accounts/push only moves that state into brittle shareable URLs and still requires scheduled data ingestion/generation. Seoul Open Data does provide a large free/open API surface, and TOPIS exposes traffic/open APIs, so raw-data cost is not the blocker. The blocker is product economics/distribution: a static district digest duplicates official/news notices, while the differentiated saved-corridor alert requires scheduled backend/channel operations and competes with existing real-time transit/navigation utilities. An RSS/static daily-generation variant would still incur recurring ingestion/quality maintenance while having weak ad/affiliate monetization and no demonstrated search-distribution wedge. This fails Lane C's near-zero-maintenance portfolio threshold; no BUILD gate is warranted.
economics: KRW0 research spend. Public data acquisition can be free, but useful personalization implies recurring scheduled processing/delivery and quality monitoring. Stateless alternatives have weak differentiation and episodic demand. Expected monthly contribution is therefore too low relative to maintenance burden; KILL rather than subsidize a low-RPM alert product with ongoing ops.
next_checkpoint: Next run: fresh genetic discovery. Prefer a stateless public-data consumer product where the data itself creates a high-intent action or recurring searchable page without requiring saved user state, push/Kakao delivery, or scheduled per-user computation.
recommendation: KILL Seoul Tomorrow Commute Disruption Digest and return to DISCOVER. Reuse the lesson, not the candidate: free public data is abundant, but Lane C should favor products whose distribution and monetization work through public/indexable surfaces rather than personalized alert infrastructure.
